title: Largest Perimeter Triangle
statement: Treat every value of `nums` as a side length. Pick three of them, from three different positions, that can be the sides of a triangle with positive area: each of the three must be strictly smaller than the sum of the other two. Return the largest perimeter (the sum of the three lengths) any such choice achieves, or `0` when no three lengths form a triangle with positive area.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every triple takes O(n³). Sorting from longest to shortest does much better. Suppose a side `c` is the longest of a triangle. The best partners for it are the next two lengths just below it in sorted order, because they give both the biggest sum (the best chance to beat `c`) and the biggest perimeter. So only consecutive triples in the sorted array need checking. The first one that passes is the answer, since perimeters only shrink further along.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in decreasing order.
2. For each `i`, take `longest = nums[i]` and `others`, the sum of the next two lengths.
3. If `longest < others`, these three form a triangle with positive area. Return `longest + others` straight away.
4. If no window passes, return `0`.

The other two triangle inequalities hold on their own, because `longest` is at least as big as each of the other two.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 1, 2]` sorts to `[2, 2, 1]`. With `i = 0`, `longest = 2` and `others = 2 + 1 = 3`. Since `2 < 3`, the triangle is valid and the answer is `2 + 3 = 5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort, which works in place.

## Pitfalls

- The inequality must be strict: `1, 1, 2` has zero area and does not count.
- JavaScript's default `sort()` compares values as text, so pass a numeric comparator.
- If the longest side fails with its two nearest neighbours, it fails with every other pair too, so move on to the next `i` without trying other partners.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | index of the longest side in the current window of three |
| `longest` | the length at `nums[i]` |
| `others` | sum of the two lengths right after it |

narration.2: Sort the lengths from longest to shortest.
narration.3: Slide a window of three consecutive lengths down the sorted array.
narration.4: The first length of the window is the longest side.
narration.5: Add the two next-longest lengths, the best partners it can have.
narration.6: A triangle has positive area exactly when the longest side is shorter than the other two together.
narration.7: The first valid window has the biggest perimeter, so return it.
narration.10: No window works, so no triangle exists; return 0.
